unit.label: Numbers & everyday prices
unit.title: How Much Altogether?
unit.description: 13 new words and forms. Build numbers up to 99, read drink prices, and ask how much one item or a whole order costs.
unit.bookReference: A Course in Contemporary Chinese 1 · Lesson 4 請問一共多少錢？ · prices and totals pp. 66–67; money measure pp. 70–71; number-building p. 80 (through 99 here).

lessons.title: Two, Three, Four
lessons.subtitle: Name the numbers and count cups.

steps.explanation: sì is four, with a falling fourth tone.

steps.prompt: Which number is 3?
steps.explanation: 三, sān, is three.

steps.prompt: You want two cups of tea. Which familiar form counts the two cups?
steps.explanation: Use 兩 before 杯 for two cups. 二 names the number two.

lessons.title: Five, Six, Seven
lessons.subtitle: Keep the quantity and pronunciation clear.

steps.explanation: liù is six.

steps.prompt: A group orders 7 cups of tea. Which quantity matches?
steps.explanation: 七 is seven. Keep 杯 between the number and the drink.

lessons.title: Eight, Nine, Ten—and Beyond
lessons.subtitle: Use tens and ones to build numbers up to 99.

steps.explanation: shí, ten, has a rising tone; sì, four, has a falling tone.

steps.prompt: Which number is 23?
steps.explanation: 二十 is twenty, plus 三 makes twenty-three.

steps.prompt: Which number is 40, with no extra ones?
steps.explanation: Four tens is 四十. 十四 is ten plus four: fourteen.

steps.prompt: How do you read 99?
steps.explanation: Nine tens plus nine ones: 九十 + 九.

steps.prompt: Which correctly pairs twenty with two cups?
steps.explanation: Use 二 in 二十, twenty. Keep 兩 before 杯 for two cups.

lessons.title: Read a Price
lessons.subtitle: Money, dollars, and the amount after an item.

steps.prompt: In 一杯茶三十五塊, what does 三十五 tell you?
steps.explanation: The price comes before 塊. 一杯 gives the cup count.

steps.prompt: Do 四十塊 and 四十塊錢 give the same price?
steps.explanation: 錢 is optional after the money measure 塊.

steps.prompt: The price label reads 六十五塊. How much is that?
steps.explanation: 六十 is sixty; add 五 for sixty-five.

steps.prompt: Choose the medium cup size, using Unit 11.
steps.explanation: 中杯 is a size. 三杯 and 六杯 are quantities.

lessons.title: How Much Is It?
lessons.subtitle: Ask a price and recognize the answer.

steps.explanation: duōshǎo means how much or how many; 多少錢 asks a price.

steps.prompt: A friend asks 這杯茶多少錢？ Which reply gives a price?
steps.explanation: An amount followed by 塊 gives the price. The other replies give quantity or size.

steps.prompt: Which is the price question practiced here?
steps.explanation: 多少 already asks for the missing amount. Do not add 嗎.

lessons.title: How Much Altogether?
lessons.subtitle: Combine prices and complete a purchase.

steps.prompt: Practice menu: tea NT$35, coffee NT$40. One of each costs how much altogether?
steps.explanation: 35 + 40 = 75, 七十五. 一共 asks for the total.

steps.prompt: Tea is NT$35 per cup. You buy two cups. Which statement matches?
steps.explanation: Two cups at 35 each total 70: 35 + 35.

steps.prompt: You have ordered a tea and a coffee. Which question asks for the entire bill?
steps.explanation: 一共 asks for all the ordered items together.

steps.prompt: You hear “一共七十五塊.” What is the total?
steps.explanation: 七十五 is seven tens and five ones.

steps.prompt: The staff asks 外帶還是內用？ You are taking the drinks away. Reply.
steps.explanation: 外帶 answers the service question. 多少錢 asks a different question.

lessons.title: Unit Challenge
lessons.subtitle: Numbers, prices, and the full order. No new material.

steps.explanation: liù means six.
shí is ten; sì is four.

steps.prompt: Which written number means 68?
steps.explanation: Six tens plus eight ones: 60 + 8.

steps.prompt: Which written number means 94?
steps.explanation: Nine tens plus four ones: 90 + 4.

steps.prompt: Which part of 三十五塊錢 is the everyday money measure?
steps.explanation: 塊 is the money measure; 錢 means money, and 三十五 is the amount.

steps.prompt: How do you ask the price of one cup of tea?
steps.explanation: Use the item followed by 多少錢, without 嗎.

steps.prompt: A tea costs NT$25 and a coffee NT$40. One of each costs what altogether?
steps.explanation: 25 + 40 = 65, 六十五. These are the prices given in this question.

steps.prompt: Each coffee costs NT$40. Two cups cost what?
You want two cups. Which expression gives the quantity?
steps.explanation: 兩杯 counts two cups. 二十塊 is a price.

newVocabulary.note: Names the number two. Keep 兩 before 杯 for two cups.

newVocabulary.meaning: dollar; measure word for everyday prices
newVocabulary.note: In this unit’s Taiwan shop examples, prices are in New Taiwan dollars.
Here, 多少錢 asks a price. The two characters make one question word.
一 is pronounced yí before the fourth tone in 共.

二.note: 二 names the number two. When counting two cups, keep the familiar 兩杯. Learn 二 for naming the number itself.
二.memory: Two separate horizontal lines: the upper line is shorter, the lower line wider.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: upper horizontal
parts.description: Write the shorter upper line first, leaving space beneath it.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: lower horizontal
parts.description: Write the longer lower line underneath; the two lines never touch.

三.note: 三 names the number three. 三杯茶 is three cups of tea.
三.memory: Three separate horizontal lines: the middle is shortest and the bottom is widest.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: top horizontal
parts.description: Write the upper horizontal first. Keep it separate from the middle line.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: middle horizontal
parts.description: The second horizontal is shorter. Leave a clear gap above and below it.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: bottom horizontal
parts.description: Finish with the longest horizontal to give 三 a broad base.

四.note: 四 names the number four. Its pronunciation sì has a falling fourth tone.
四.memory: 四 has an outer box around two inner strokes. Close the bottom of the box last.

parts.label: 囗
parts.name: outer enclosure
parts.description: Start with the left side and the hooked top-right side. The bottom horizontal closes the enclosure after the inside is written.

parts.label: 儿
parts.name: inner strokes
parts.description: Inside the box, write a left-falling stroke and a bent stroke. Keep them clear of the outer sides.

五.note: 五 names the number five. 五杯茶 is five cups of tea.
五.memory: 五 has a short upper bar, a descending inner stroke, a bent middle stroke, and a broad bottom bar.

parts.label: 五
parts.name: 五 strokes
parts.description: Write the top horizontal, the descending stroke, the horizontal-turn stroke, then the long bottom horizontal. The third stroke turns downward on the right.

六.note: 六 names the number six. Keep its falling fourth tone: liù.
六.memory: 六 has a dot and a long horizontal above two spreading lower strokes.

parts.label: 亠
parts.name: top dot and bar
parts.description: Write the top dot, then the horizontal underneath it.

parts.label: 八
parts.name: lower strokes
parts.description: Finish with the left-falling stroke and the short right-hand dot. They spread apart below the bar.

七.note: 七 names the number seven. Its high first tone is qī.
七.memory: 七 crosses a rising horizontal with a vertical that bends right into a hook.

parts.label: 七
parts.name: 七 strokes
parts.description: Write the slightly rising horizontal first. The second stroke drops through it, turns right, and finishes with a small hook.

八.note: 八 names the number eight. The two strokes separate rather than meeting at the top.
八.memory: 八 opens outward: a shorter left-falling stroke and a longer right-falling stroke.

parts.label: 八
parts.name: 八 strokes
parts.description: Write the left-falling stroke first and the right-falling stroke second. Leave a gap between their upper ends.

九.note: 九 names the number nine. Pronounce it jiǔ, with third tone.
九.memory: 九 starts with a curved left-falling stroke. Its second stroke crosses it, turns down, and hooks up at the lower right.

parts.label: 九
parts.name: 九 strokes
parts.description: Write the left-falling stroke first. Then draw the short horizontal into a downward curve and finish the hooked turn.

十.note: 十 names ten. Its rising tone shí is different from the falling sì of 四.
十.memory: 十 is a simple cross. The vertical passes through the horizontal and extends above and below it.

parts.label: 十
parts.name: 十 strokes
parts.description: Write the horizontal first. Write one vertical through it, keeping the crossing near the middle.

錢.note: 錢 means money. After a price such as 三十五塊, it is optional: 三十五塊錢 gives the same price.
錢.memory: 錢 places the metal component 金 on the left and two stacked 戈 shapes on the right.

parts.label: 金
parts.name: metal component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form the narrow metal component. Its top opens into a cover above the lower bars and dots.

parts.label: 戔
parts.name: stacked right-hand component
parts.description: Two four-stroke 戈 shapes are stacked on the right. Keep their long slanting hooks and small dots distinct.

塊.note: 塊 follows an amount in everyday prices. In these Taiwan drink-shop examples, 三十塊 means NT$30.
塊.memory: 塊 has 土 on the left and 鬼 on the right. The right side is much wider than the three-stroke 土.

parts.label: 土
parts.name: earth component
parts.description: Write the small horizontal, vertical, and rising lower stroke on the left.

parts.label: 鬼
parts.name: right-hand component
parts.description: The ten strokes of 鬼 begin with a short slant over a box, then continue into the curved lower strokes and small inner mark.

多.meaning: first syllable of 多少, how much/how many
多.note: 多 begins 多少. Learn 多少 as one question word here; do not translate the characters separately.
多.memory: 多 stacks two 夕 shapes. The lower one sits slightly farther to the right.

parts.label: 夕
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: The first three strokes form the upper 夕: a short slant, a longer bent stroke, and an inner mark.

parts.label: 夕
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: Repeat the three-stroke 夕 below, leaving room between the two components.

少.meaning: final syllable of 多少, how much/how many
少.note: 少 completes 多少. Keep the third tone in duōshǎo.
少.memory: 少 resembles 小 with an extra long left-falling stroke below. That last stroke sweeps under the upper marks.

parts.label: 小
parts.name: upper strokes
parts.description: Write the short central vertical and the two side marks at the top.

parts.label: 丿
parts.name: long final stroke
parts.description: Finish with a long left-falling stroke that begins on the right and sweeps underneath the upper strokes.

共.note: 共 completes 一共, altogether. In this expression 一 is pronounced yí before the fourth-tone gòng.
共.memory: 共 has two upright strokes through two horizontal bars, with two short spreading strokes below.

parts.label: 龷
parts.name: upper structure
parts.description: Write the upper horizontal, the two verticals, then the wider lower horizontal across them.

parts.label: 八
parts.name: lower strokes
parts.description: Finish with the two spreading lower strokes, leaving a gap below the upper structure.

u12-small-numbers.title: Numbers two, three and four
u12-small-numbers.pattern: 一 → 二 → 三 → 四
u12-small-numbers.explanation: You know 一, one. Add 二 èr, two; 三 sān, three; and 四 sì, four. These name numbers in a counting sequence. When you count things, keep the measure word: 三杯茶 is three cups of tea. For two cups, use the familiar 兩杯茶. 二 names the number two; 兩 is the form already learned before a measure word.

examples.pinyin: liǎng bēi chá, sān bēi chá, sì bēi chá
examples.meaning: two cups of tea, three cups of tea, four cups of tea

u12-small-numbers.remember: Name 2 as 二; count two cups as 兩杯.

u12-middle-numbers.title: Numbers five, six and seven
u12-middle-numbers.explanation: Continue the sequence with 五 wǔ, five; 六 liù, six; and 七 qī, seven. Their tones differ: wǔ is third tone, liù is fourth, and qī is first. You can put each number before the already-known 杯 to count cups. A number answers how many, not the drink’s size.
u12-middle-numbers.remember: 五 = 5, 六 = 6, 七 = 7. Keep 杯 between the number and the drink.

u12-to-ten.title: Numbers eight, nine and ten
u12-to-ten.explanation: Finish the basic sequence: 八 bā is eight, 九 jiǔ is nine, and 十 shí is ten. Listen carefully to 四 sì, four, and 十 shí, ten: both the initial sound and the tone differ. 十 will also be the building block for tens.
u12-to-ten.remember: 八 = 8, 九 = 9, 十 = 10. 四 sì and 十 shí are different numbers.

u12-tens.title: Build numbers from 11 to 99
u12-tens.pattern: 十 + ones; digit + 十 + optional ones
u12-tens.explanation: Chinese builds these numbers by place value. 十一 is ten plus one, 11. 十二 is ten plus two, 12. For 20, say 二十: two tens. 二十三 is two tens plus three, 23. 三十五 is three tens plus five, 35. If there are no extra ones, stop after 十: 四十 is 40. Do not read 35 as 三五; that names two separate digits. Use 二 inside these numbers, such as 二十 and 三十二. Use 兩 to count two cups: 兩杯. This lesson practices whole numbers through 99.
u12-tens.remember: Before 十: how many tens. After 十: extra ones. 二十三 = 20 + 3, not 3 + 20 in reversed order.

u12-price.title: Say a price
u12-price.explanation: 錢, qián, means money. 塊, kuài, is the everyday money measure after an amount. In these Taiwan shop examples, 三十五塊 means NT$35. 三十五塊錢 gives the same amount; 錢 is optional after 塊. You can state a simple price directly: 一杯茶三十五塊. The number after the drink gives the price; the number before 杯 gives the quantity. These prices are practice examples, not a current shop menu.

examples.meaning: One cup of tea costs NT$35.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bēi kāfēi sìshí kuài qián.
examples.meaning: This cup of coffee costs NT$40.

u12-price.remember: Cup count: number + 杯. Price: amount + 塊, with optional 錢.

u12-price-question.title: Ask how much it costs
u12-price-question.explanation: 多少, duōshǎo, means how much or how many. Here, 多少錢 asks how much money: the price. Put the item first: 一杯茶多少錢？ If the item is already clear, 多少錢？ is enough. Do not add 嗎: 多少 already asks for the missing amount. Answer with the price, such as 三十五塊. This question asks a price, not how many cups you want.

examples.meaning: How much is one cup of tea?

examples.pinyin: Zhè bēi rè kāfēi duōshǎo qián?
examples.meaning: How much is this cup of hot coffee?

u12-price-question.remember: 多少錢 asks the price. Answer with an amount + 塊. No 嗎 is needed.

u12-total.title: Ask for the whole order
u12-total.pattern: 一共 + amount + 塊; 一共多少錢？
u12-total.explanation: 一共, yígòng, means altogether or in total. Place it before the total amount: 一共七十五塊. If one cup of tea is 35 and one cup of coffee is 40, the whole order is 75: 35 + 40 = 75. 一共多少錢？ asks for this combined amount. 一共 does not mean everyone; it totals the order. In this expression 一 is pronounced yí before fourth-tone gòng.

examples.text: 一杯茶三十五塊，一杯咖啡四十塊，一共七十五塊。
examples.pinyin: Yì bēi chá sānshíwǔ kuài, yì bēi kāfēi sìshí kuài, yígòng qīshíwǔ kuài.
examples.meaning: One tea costs NT$35 and one coffee costs NT$40; the total is NT$75.

u12-total.remember: Use 一共 for the combined price. Here 35 + 40 = 七十五.

u12-three-teas.meaning: I would like three cups of tea.
u12-three-teas.note: Three is 三; the familiar cup measure follows.

u12-four-coffees.meaning: I would like four cups of coffee.

u12-six-teas.meaning: I would like six cups of tea.
u12-six-teas.note: 六 changes the quantity, not the cup size.

u12-tea-price.meaning: One cup of tea costs NT$35.
u12-tea-price.note: One is the cup count; thirty-five is the price.

u12-coffee-price.pinyin: Zhè bēi kāfēi sìshí kuài qián.
u12-coffee-price.meaning: This cup of coffee costs NT$40.
u12-coffee-price.note: 錢 is optional after 塊.

u12-ask-tea.meaning: How much is one cup of tea?
u12-ask-tea.note: 多少錢 asks for the missing price.

u12-ask-coffee.pinyin: Zhè bēi rè kāfēi duōshǎo qián?
u12-ask-coffee.meaning: How much is this cup of hot coffee?
u12-ask-coffee.note: Ask about the specific hot coffee.

u12-total-question.note: The order is understood from context.

u12-total-answer.note: For one NT$35 tea and one NT$40 coffee, 35 + 40 = 75.

u12-two-teas-total.pinyin: Liǎng bēi chá yígòng qīshí kuài.
u12-two-teas-total.meaning: Two cups of tea cost NT$70 altogether.
u12-two-teas-total.note: In the practice menu, one tea is NT$35. Two cost 35 + 35 = 70.

u12-price-exchange.text: 這杯茶多少錢？三十五塊。
u12-price-exchange.pinyin: Zhè bēi chá duōshǎo qián? Sānshíwǔ kuài.
u12-price-exchange.meaning: How much is this cup of tea? NT$35.
u12-price-exchange.note: A price question followed by its amount answer.
